v.why: Replacing a missing edge can reconnect input to output, which gives a much larger gain than swapping one existing op for another (e.g. +78 in run 79).
Adding a direct 0->3 path where none existed restores connectivity, whereas replacing a conv with skip often hurts.
With edge 3 absent, removing edge 4 can cut the only route to the output (runs 57, 59 lose 70+ points).
If edge 5 is also none, node 3 is reachable only through edge 4, so removing it disconnects the cell.
When edge 4 is absent, edge 3 is a critical path to the output, so upgrading it matters more.
Replacing a parameter-free pool with a conv gives a large gain in the pool-dominated cell (run 13: +37).
Replacing a parameter-free pool with a conv gives a large gain (run 33: +35), unlike replacing a conv.
In cells dominated by skip connections, adding a learnable 3x3 conv on edge 0 gives large gains on all datasets (run 2: +43).
Replacing a parameter-free skip with a 3x3 conv helps more than replacing an existing conv (run 82: +35).
Replacing a pooling edge with a 3x3 conv adds learnable capacity, giving a large gain (runs 73 and 78).
